assertion_review.note: This node is a measurement role: it adds no product assertion, so there is no added assertion to weigh against an independent source. Its publication is the added-failure delta, and that delta is falsifiable by the two logs it cites — I reproduced it from the logs directly, not from the manifest's summary. The change under test (571f4e8cc) does add a guard (require_qualified_axis(admitted) at nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py:3327) plus a test edit in tests/test_fused_same_state_read.py, but that guard and test belong to the fused-route node, not to this test-role node, and are outside this review's diff.

findings.text: follow-on: the recorded after_suite.command is the launcher argv ('.../scripts/h200_test_lane/run.sh --log <run>/head-reference-full.log --time 02:00:00 -- tests/test_equilibrium_forward_reference.py'), but the command that actually ran is the one the head log header prints at its COMMAND line: '.../python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_equilibrium_forward_reference.py --timeout 3600'. The manifest's baseline_suite.command carries an explicit '--timeout 3600' because the base revision's launcher predates the per-test bound, so the two recorded commands differ in whether the bound appears even though both logs' pytest headers read 'timeout: 3600.0s'. The measure is unaffected (test outcomes only), but a reader comparing the two stored command fields can read them as running under different timeouts when they did not.

follow-on: both arms ran against a prewarm pin compiled for another revision (each log carries PINNED_REVISION_MISMATCH pinned=eb565ed4...), so the two wall times (976.26s, 967.42s) are compile-affected and are not a comparable timing measurement; the report and manifest record this correctly and exclude timing from the measure, but the numeric walls appear in the report's arms table and could be lifted from it into a millisecond-cost claim they cannot support. This run produces a test-outcome delta only; no wall-clock evidence for the §3 figure is present in these two logs.

gate_arms_note: Both arms are present and readable in the reviewed run's own manifest. baseline_suite (revision d786948c4) and after_suite (revision 0e5e34157) each declare completed true, exit_status 1, failure_count 8 and an eight-element failure_ids list. I derived the delta twice and both derivations agree: from the manifest's stored ids (set(after) - set(baseline) is empty) and independently from the reviewed run's own gate logs, whose FAILED lines I parsed directly (head-reference-full.log: 8 FAILED lines; base-reference-full.log: 8 FAILED lines; the sorted sets are identical), so added_failure_ids is empty by a measured absence rather than an omitted comparison. Positive control for that absence: the same parser sees eight FAILED ids and the terminal summary line '8 failed, 21 passed' in each log, so it demonstrably reads a non-empty failure set present in the input; the reviewed-run manifest's baseline_suite/after_suite ids are byte-equal to the log-derived ids (set equality true for both arms). A timed-out test would appear as a 'Timeout' section, of which there are zero in both logs; ERROR counts are zero in both.
